correctness.rationale: Using the stated composition order, e_ab e_cd is nonempty iff b=c, and then equals e_ad. If both products are nonempty and equal, the arrows coincide. Thus for distinct arrows adjacency is b≠c and d≠a; inclusion–exclusion gives (AX)_ab=S-R_b-C_a+X_ba-(1-δ_ab)X_ab. The last term is essential for the simple graph. This action preserves the real symmetric and skew-symmetric subspaces. On skew arrays it is R_a-R_b-2X_ab; the row sum is multiplied by n-2 and ranges onto zero-sum vectors by X_ab=(r_a-r_b)/n. The row-sum kernel has scalar -2 and dimension (n-1)(n-2)/2. On symmetric arrays the map X→(R,d) is onto: with prescribed diagonal, the orthogonal complement to the image of the unsigned off-diagonal incidence matrix consists of u_a+u_b=0 for all distinct a,b, hence is zero for n>=3. Its kernel is annihilated and has dimension n(n-3)/2. On the image, row sums update by (n-1)S-nR+d and diagonal by S-2R+d. The constant block has trace (n-1)² and determinant (n-1)(n-2); the zero-sum block, repeated n-1 times, has trace 1-n and determinant -(n-2). The blocks exhaust n² coordinates, proving the polynomial. Reality follows from real symmetry. The constant block contributes two positives and the zero-sum block one positive and one negative per copy, yielding exactly the stated inertia, rank and nullity. Nonsingularity at n=3 and singularity for n>=4 are within the claimed range; the symmetric map's surjectivity argument does not extend to n=2. The saved checker output (n=3..6, exact polynomials) and source were inspected, not run; the real all-index argument is independent of that evidence.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Let Δ project onto diagonal words aa. The looped annihilation matrix is A+I-Δ, not a scalar shift. If D counts directed length-two de Bruijn arcs, their underlying simple adjacency is D+Dᵀ-P-Δ, where P reverses each two-letter word, removing duplicate reciprocal arcs once (including the diagonal intersection); Δ then removes the remaining self-loops. The reported spectrum of D+Dᵀ alone does not determine the effect of these corrections, and Δ is not a commuting scalar on the relevant spaces. Likewise the previously computed Brandt graph invariants do not give the symmetric/skew quotient eigenvalues. The required new calculation concludes both exact factors and the sharp zero multiplicity.

evidence: Kumar–Dalal–Pandey, p. 2 or HTML offset 4009 onward, define the aperiodic Brandt semigroup with exactly this matrix-unit multiplication. Mapping e_ab to (a,1,b) and adjoining the empty map as zero is a multiplicative bijection; deleting zero gives a graph isomorphism.
Two-letter words ab and cd are adjacent in the underlying simple de Bruijn graph precisely when distinct and b=c or d=a. This makes it exactly the complement, not the commuting graph itself.

originality.rationale: The graph itself is explicitly known as the nonzero trivial-group Brandt commuting graph; its complement is the underlying simple length-two de Bruijn graph. The distinct claim supported is the explicit real spectrum and inertia with the required loop and multiplicity conventions. Neither the known Brandt graph invariants, the conventional symmetrized multigraph de Bruijn spectra nor the available mutual-annihilation spectral formulas supply that polynomial. One same-day Heisenberg record calls the matrix-unit spectrum known without an identifiable separate source; the inspected evidence does not independently substantiate that statement.
residual_risks: The Heisenberg record's attribution is unresolved and a separate unindexed spectral result under the matrix-unit alias could exist.

A separate formula for the loopless, unweighted de Bruijn graph (with reciprocal arcs merged) would likely imply the result, but the examined known spectra are not for that matrix. The inaccessible Delorme–Tillich original was compared by way of its reproduced theorem, not excluded in every passage.

value.rationale: The rank-one stratum is the intrinsic first nonzero Green class and a canonical all-index graph family, not an arbitrary subgraph. The spectral decomposition of its actual simple adjacency explains exactly which symmetric arrow modes become null and when, giving a precise baseline for comparison with group-labelled Brandt extensions and with looped semigroup relations. The value is the full set of eigenvalues with multiplicities and sharp rank transition, not renaming a known graph or tabulating small cases.
